business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retailing of Smart IoT Devices and Home Automation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 19-23, 28-32, 58-63, 78-79, 93-107, 159-197, 210-217, and 273-277; Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and its CIRCE/DUE procedures; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office, coordinated through the Colegio de Registradores de España; CIRCE may be used through an authorized Punto de Atención al Emprendedor.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, followed by registration with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry. The Unified Electronic Document (Documento Único Electrónico, DUE) may transmit applicable registrations and tax notifications.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders bear additional statutory liability in insolvency up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital. Spanish law does not require a capital escrow account. For cash contributions, a bank certificate may be provided; for an SL, founders may instead assume joint liability for the existence and reality of cash contributions where legally permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and confirms the subscription and full payment of its share capital by the incorporator(s) in accordance with the deed of incorporation and articles; (2) the registered office is adopted at [full Spanish address], with authority to notify the Mercantile Registry and tax authorities; (3) [name] is appointed [sole director/joint director/board chair], and [names] are appointed as applicable officers, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) the appointed representative is authorized to execute filings, obtain the NIF, open bank accounts, and complete all incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name and verify corporate availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identifying the intended legal form as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Obtain the negative name certificate, verify that the name remains valid for execution of the deed, and reserve it for the statutory period. Use the exact certified name in all incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry
Power of attorney, if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit alternative names or an amended name request. If the certificate expires, obtain a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain foreign investor identification and appoint a Spanish tax representative where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-Spanish individual director or shareholder and an NIF for each non-Spanish corporate shareholder before or in connection with incorporation. Foreign public documents must be apostilled or legalized and accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation. File through an authorized representative using the applicable AEAT forms and powers of attorney.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate registry certificate, if applicable
Apostilled or legalized powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identification inconsistencies, replace defective legalization or translation, and resubmit through AEAT or an authorized representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected for the registered office or incorporation process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the name certificate, articles of association, shareholder details, capital allocation, management structure, registered office evidence, beneficial ownership information, and foreign-document formalities. Execute the public deed before the notary. Pay the subscribed capital through a Spanish bank account or use the legally available founder-liability declaration for an SL. Ensure all directors accept appointment in the deed or by attached statement.
required_dossiers: Evidence of registered office or right of use
Bank certificate or permitted cash-contribution declaration
Apostilled powers and sworn translations, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify the draft deed before signature. If the notary identifies a formal defect, provide corrected documents, updated certificates, or an amended deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and submit census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), through the electronic tax portal or authorized Punto de Atención al Emprendedor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation deed or the applicable electronic incorporation data to request the provisional NIF and register the company for tax purposes. Complete the census declaration using Form 036, identify the economic activity and registered office, and select the appropriate VAT and corporate tax obligations. The permanent NIF follows after registration evidence is submitted.
required_dossiers: Notarial incorporation deed or CIRCE/DUE data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEAT requests, correct Form 036 data, and resubmit the deed or identification documents through the same filing channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic or paper copy of the public deed, articles, provisional NIF, name certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and required registry forms. Pay the applicable registry and publication charges. Monitor the registry entry and obtain the registration certificate, permanent NIF evidence, and legalized or certified copies of the registered deed.
required_dossiers: Registry application and fee payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a qualification notice is issued, cure each stated defect within the applicable period by filing corrected documents, an additional deed, or a response to the registrar. Appeal or seek judicial review where legally appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate, municipal, and employment registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, relevant municipality, General Treasury of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and applicable regional labor authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Replace the provisional NIF with the permanent NIF, confirm census and VAT registrations, legalize required accounting and corporate books electronically, obtain the municipal activity or opening authorization where required, register as an employer before hiring, and enroll employees in Social Security. Establish accounting, invoicing, data protection, product compliance, and beneficial ownership recordkeeping controls.
required_dossiers: Director and employee Social Security documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal or Social Security queries, supplement technical documents, correct activity codes, and appeal an adverse administrative decision within the applicable statutory deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general national industrial manufacturing license is required for ordinary retailing of smart-home IoT hardware. If the company operates a warehouse, installs equipment, undertakes electrical work, or conducts manufacturing, the competent authority is the relevant Autonomous Community industrial authority, together with the municipality issuing the activity or opening authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal declaration of responsible activity (declaración responsable de actividad) or municipal opening and operating license (licencia de apertura y funcionamiento), as determined by the applicable municipality and activity classification. A manufacturing or regulated technical installation would require the applicable regional industrial registration or authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and the framework of the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally Exempt for ordinary retail premises and standard storage of packaged IoT products without manufacturing, significant emissions, hazardous waste treatment, or regulated installations. A screening determination or full or simplified EIA may apply if the premises or project falls within the statutory annexes or regional environmental legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or material VOC emissions should arise from ordinary retail operations. Any wastewater discharge must comply with municipal or basin-authority authorization and applicable discharge limits. Packaging, batteries, electronic equipment, and other regulated waste must be segregated and transferred to authorized waste managers under Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils. Products containing batteries or electrical and electronic equipment trigger applicable extended producer responsibility, registration, labeling, and take-back obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain any required municipal fire-safety and opening authorization based on premises size, occupancy, storage load, and local ordinance. Fire installations must comply with Royal Decree 513/2017 on fire protection installations, and applicable buildings must comply with the Technical Building Code. Verify structural floor loads for warehouse shelving and stored equipment. Before hiring, implement occupational risk prevention under Law 31/1995, including risk assessment, emergency planning, worker information and training, and coordination with external prevention services where required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica — sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs/EORI: Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales (AEAT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Execute deed of incorporation before a notary and file with Registro Mercantil; 2) Apply to AEAT for definitive corporate NIF via Form 036/037, presenting deed, appointment of director and Spanish tax address; 3) Register in Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores declaring commencement of activity; 4) Obtain NIF-IVA (VAT registration) confirmation and, for exports/imports, an EORI number; 5) Obtain a digital certificate (Certificado Electrónico) or Cl@ve PIN for mandatory electronic filings. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment must apply for a non-resident NIF (Form 036) before acquiring Spanish real property or engaging in taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election in Spanish law; an SL is mandatorily an entity-level resident taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 (LIS). Available elections: (i) reduced 15% CIT rate for first two tax periods with positive tax base (new-company relief); (ii) group tax consolidation regime (arts. 55–79 LIS) for parent-subsidiary groups holding ≥70%; (iii) VAT One-Stop-Shop (OSS/IOSS) registration for intra-community distance sales and imports; (iv) pago fraccionado (corporate income tax instalment) calculation-method election; (v) voluntary SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) real-time VAT ledger submission.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido — IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold: any entrepreneur or professional habitually performing taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register for IVA regardless of turnover. Non-established EU sellers register via OSS once intra-EU distance sales exceed EUR 10,000 in the preceding or current calendar year; non-EU sellers have no threshold. Physical retail of IoT hardware in Spain is always taxable at 21%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B electronic invoicing mandated by Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 18/2022) for all entrepreneurs/professionals with a Spanish tax address; Verifactu (RD 1007/2023) requires certified invoicing and billing software capable of generating compliant e-invoice JSON/XML records and making them accessible to AEAT; taxpayers in the SII regime (turnover above EUR 6 million) must submit invoice records in near-real-time (4/8 days) to AEAT in XML format via web services (API). No full real-time dependent clearance or digital stamping is yet operational for SME retailers, but fiscal records must be continuously available for AEAT inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods dispatched to destinations outside the EU (Art. 21 Ley 37/1992) where the seller retains possession/documentary control and ships the goods within 3 months of supply; for intra-EU B2B supplies, the supply is exempt with right to deduction where the customer communicates a valid NIF-IVA and the goods are transported to another member state; IoT hardware sold to final consumers in other EU states through the OSS is taxed at destination-member-state rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) — export customs entry accepted and validated by AEAT Customs, including MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Transport contract evidence: Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill naming seller as exporter and third-country destination
Commercial invoice with Incoterms indicating transfer of risk/ownership abroad (e.g., EXW / FOB / CIF)
Proof of payment / inward remittance certificate or bank transfer confirmation of export consideration (for FX substantiation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT frequently audits export zero-rating claims, requiring complete documentary chain and proof of physical exit within the statutory period; unjustified zero-rating triggers immediate VAT clawback plus late-payment interest (Art. 170 Ley 37/1992; Arts. 191–194 Ley 58/2003), penalties of 50%–150% of the omitted tax base in fraud cases, and loss of deduction rights; deliberate export-fraud (carousel/missing-trader) or false documentation can constitute criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with potential imprisonment of 1–6 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the national competent authority for monetary policy, banking supervision, and external transactions statistics, in coordination with the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for foreign investment declarations and the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) for securities-linked capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully liberalized exchange system under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Directive 88/361/EEC. Both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible; there are no exchange controls or prior authorization requirements for inward or outward remittances. Profit and dividend remittance is unrestricted, subject only to standard corporate income tax treatment (with possible 19% withholding for non-EU exiting equityholders, reduced or eliminated under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable double tax treaties). Residual compliance burdens are procedural: (i) statistical Balance of Payments declarations to Banco de España for external transactions aggregating ≥ EUR 50,000 per counter-party per year (EUR 1,000,000 for financial transactions) via the 'Data' electronic reporting system; and (ii) foreign investment registry filing to the Ministry of Economy for non-resident equity investments of ≥ 10% or amounts above EUR 3,000,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spanish law (Royal Decree 1816/1991) imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may retain export receipts freely in EUR or foreign currency and apply them to working capital, investment, or onward disbursements. Only statistical Balance of Payments reporting obligations apply to export payments, recorded under the applicable BoP service or goods codes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Spanish and EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions (authorized by Banco de España under Ley 21/2011 and PSD2, or passporting into Spain from another EEA state) are viable partners for euro-denominated payment routing, virtual IBANs, and cross-border multi-currency settlement, but are generally unsuitable as exclusive holders of capital escrow or corporate treasury cash due to narrower prudential buffers and limited FX counterparty capacity. Post-Brexit UK EMIs have lost EU passporting rights and may only operate in Spain through a Spanish branch, a subsidiary, or reliance on a Spanish/EU clearing partner. Unlicensed offshore EMIs are not viable and expose the entity to unregulated funds-holding risk under Spanish AML law.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically; Ley 10/2010 permits non-face-to-face identification through qualified electronic signatures, video identification, or notarial certification. However, tier-1 Spanish banks, as a matter of internal risk policy, typically require (i) a physical or notarially certified appointment of a local authorized representative (apoderado), (ii) apostilled corporate documents, and (iii) an in-person or video interview of the ultimate beneficial owner for non-resident corporate clients. Remote opening is practically possible for an EU-resident director with a Spanish tax ID (NIF) and an advanced e-signature, but a local resident representative materially accelerates onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque beneficial ownership chain involving non-EU ultimate owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Certificate of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) and registered bylaws; 2. Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titularidad Real) or equivalent UBO declaration; 3. Simplified ownership diagram identifying each natural person above 25% threshold; 4. Notarized and apostilled passports of all UBOs; 5. Current company tax residence certificate (Residencia Fiscal); 6. Entity-level explanation of commercial rationale for the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared activities (E-commerce IoT retail) and actual transaction flow (high-value, multi-jurisdiction trade payments)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Executed distribution / supply contracts with major IoT hardware vendors; 2. Marketplace agreements (e.g., Shopify, Stripe) evidencing digital retail operations; 3. Twelve-month transaction forecasting and pro-forma invoices; 4. Past corporate income tax returns or audited financials (if available); 5. Warehouse or logistics agreements proving physical fulfillment chain; 6. Product catalog, trade licenses (if any), and ISIC code confirmation letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a high-risk or cash-intensive jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Source-of-funds declaration for the injection amount; 2. Bank statement of the originating account for the last 6 months; 3. Underlying shareholder loan agreement or board resolution approving the capital contribution; 4. Evidence of the originator's business activity (contracts, employer letter, sale deeds, or liquidation statements); 5. Tax clearance certificate from the originator's tax authority where available; 6. Legal opinion or certificate of solvency for large institutional investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) with no operating history and funds arriving immediately after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Detailed business plan with market analysis, revenue model, and funding forecast for the SL; 2. Founder resumes and notices of the beneficial owners; 3. Escrow/term sheet confirming purpose of the initial injection; 4. Confirmation that minimum share capital (EUR 1.00 per statutory option or full EUR 3,000 paid) has been duly subscribed; 5. Definitive cross-border supply agreements and EU market entry strategy documents; 6. Commitment letter for audited financial statements within the first fiscal cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High frequency of cross-border inbound wire transfers triggering repeated balance of payments scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1. Consolidated schedule of all expected inbound remittances with purpose codes and supporting contracts; 2. Harmonized external transaction declaration (BoP) confirmations filed with Banco de España; 3. Intercompany agreements and transfer pricing documentation; 4. Director's board minutes approving each funding tranche; 5. Invoice and bill-of-lading trail confirming genuine trade or intercompany service nature of payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: for EEA-sourced EUR funding, route via SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) using the entity's IBAN. For non-EEA or foreign-currency injections (e.g., USD from Latin American investors), use SWIFT MT103 with a Sender-to-Receiver Information (Field 72) memo stating the economic purpose. Purpose/Balance of Payments coding: for direct equity contributions use BoP code 'M2 Shares and other equity participation' / Foreign Investment type 'X - capital contribution'; for shareholder loans use code 'M2 Financial loans' + 'M2 Loans - non-bank'. Required verification packets: board resolution authorizing the issuance or debt; shareholder register update; source of funds certificate; and, where applicable, Latin American remittance side declarations. The receiving Spanish bank must be given a completed 'Declaration of External Transaction' (Declaración de Transacciones Exteriores) form for flows ≥ EUR 50,000; failure to report exposes the entity to administrative fines under Royal Decree 1816/1991.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier payments outside the EEA (e.g., Asian IoT component manufacturers), routed through the entity's EUR or multi-currency account at a Spanish tier-1 bank, with purpose code 'M2 Trade credits' or 'M2 Services' and referenced trade invoices; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (Documentary Credits governed by UCP600) issued by the Spanish bank for bulk hardware procurement, with EUR or USD settlement via TARGET2 and correspondent banks; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer / SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EU-domiciled suppliers and EU logistics providers; and (iv) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV as internal cover payments where interbank correspondent chains require a second leg. Disbursements should be paired with the tax-relevant invoice trail (Factura proforma / factura definitiva) and, where applicable, ATR/SAD customs declarations to support VAT treatment and transfer pricing substance for the Spanish SL.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/MXN) — permitted without licensing for underlying trade exposure; executed through an authorized Spanish credit institution under the ISDA/EMTN master agreement.
FX Spot transactions for operational conversion of USD revenue from the connected market (e.g., Latin American e-commerce flows) into EUR; no regulatory restriction for spot trades of lesser amount.

Cross-Currency Swap (EUR/USD) — permissible for hedging procurement liabilities in USD-denominated hardware supply contracts, executed with a bank counterparty subject to Banque de España margin requirements.
Currency Options (European-style, EUR put / USD call or EUR call / USD put) — permitted for protecting revenue conversion floors on high-ticket smart-home IoT purchases.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — not standard for EUR (fully convertible) but available infrequently for exotic Latin American currencies as cash-settled hedges where deliverability is impossible; if used, requires documented illiquidity justification and board approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) for the SL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil del domicilio social (Spanish Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within 6 months of year-end (30 June for calendar-year SL); deposit within 1 month of approval (31 July for 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) preventing further inscriptions; administrative fines up to EUR 60,000 under LSC art. 284; no automatic strike-off for a single omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the tax year end; for calendar-year SL, no later than 25 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% plus 1% per month up to 15%; late-payment interest; penalties after formal AEAT request up to 150% of the tax due; no immediate strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January following the calendar year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges under LGT art. 27 (5% to 15%); fixed penalties for omitted or inaccurate data; no direct administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual information statement on operations with third parties (Modelo 347), if any customer or supplier transactions exceed EUR 3,000 in a year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1 March following the calendar year; not applicable where the SL's retail payment rails have no Spanish vendors/customers above the threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and possible surcharges under LGT art. 27; amounts up to EUR 10,000 for minor omissions in aggregated cases; no strike-off effect

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for an SL when, for two consecutive years, it meets at least two of: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for listed companies, groups required to file consolidated accounts, financial institutions, and entities subject to sector-specific audit rules. A shareholder holding at least 5% of the capital can request a statutory audit even below the thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts under Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad), with the PGC de Pymes regime available to qualifying reduced-size SLs. Consolidated accounts follow IFRS as adopted by the EU where applicable. Annual accounts comprise the balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, explanatory notes, and, where required, the cash-flow statement and management report.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation form for an ordinary non-listed Spanish SL. The SL must maintain a current internal UBO register (Libro Registro de Titularidad Real) and update it within 15 days of any change of control or share transfer. Share transfers must be executed by public instrument and recorded in the members register; significant ownership changes are also reflected in the annual accounts and, when a corporate tax filing is made, shareholders and directors are identified to AEAT under the Modelo 200 disclosures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Contracts with Directors (Libro Registro de Contratos con Administradores)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – USD 1,800 per year for registered office and compliance agent in Madrid or Barcelona; provincial Service Providers may be lower
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,200 – USD 7,500 for a reduced-size SL engaged in IoT hardware retail; USD 8,000 – USD 15,000 for a full statutory audit where turnover or asset thresholds are exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% base rate with deductions for R&D investments and reinvested profits up to 10%

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 CIT declaration via AEAT electronic portal

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, report only Spanish source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 100 euros per day, up to 1,500 euros, plus 20% surcharge on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC to Spanish tax authorities (AEAT) with supporting documents for reduced rate under DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19%, Interest: 19% or treaty rates (e.g. 0-10% depending on treaty)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applies to IP holding companies and certain activities; retail operations generally exempt

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 225% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal criminal liability, fines, and disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a company without economic substance or real business activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Dissolution, fines up to 300,000 euros, and potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil, personal restitution obligations, and possible imprisonment for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with anti-money laundering reporting or suspicious transaction identification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 2 million euros or 10% of annual turnover, plus criminal penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, disqualification, and potential jail time for willful non-compliance
